briefing: Good morning, Commander! You have power to share today. Where should it go?
A new sol on Mars! Check the bars, then decide how to use our power.
Rise and shine, Commander! The crew is waiting for your plan.
ok: Nice work! The base is running smoothly and the crew is happy.
Great choices! Everything is steady here at Gale Crater.
Smooth sol, Commander. Mission planners would give you a thumbs up!
warning: Careful, Commander! One of our bars is getting low. Every power choice has a cost.
Hmm, something needs attention. Look for the lowest bar.
We are okay for now, but we can't keep doing this for long.
fail: The mission had to end early. Real planners learn from every try, and so can you!
We ran out of something important. Every resource matters on Mars.
win: Mission complete! You kept the crew safe AND finished the science. Amazing!
You did it, Commander! That's exactly how real mission planners think.
tips: Life support keeps the crew breathing. Never let it run out!
The greenhouse grows food, but it needs power every sol.
The storm shield blocks the extra radiation from solar storms. Radiation is invisible energy from space.
Science is why we came, but the crew must stay safe first.
A dust storm means less sunlight, so less solar power.
NASA sets a limit on how much radiation an astronaut may get in a whole career.
Radio from Earth takes minutes to reach Mars. A Weather Station warns you faster.
A sol is one day on Mars. It is about 40 minutes longer than a day on Earth.
